categories.main_business_segments: Samyoung operates primarily in four business segments: Capacitor Film, BOPP Film, WRAP Film, and Heavy Industry. The Capacitor Film segment produces high-value ultra-thin films used in eco-friendly vehicles, renewable energy inverters, and electronic capacitors. The BOPP segment manufactures biaxially oriented polypropylene films mainly for food packaging. The WRAP segment produces plastic films such as PVC, PE, and eco-friendly PO wraps for food packaging. The Heavy Industry segment manufactures large ship engine parts through its subsidiary Samyoung Heavy Industries. The milk carton packaging segment was discontinued in 2023.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company utilizes advanced film extrusion and biaxial stretching (T-DIE process) for BOPP films and proprietary ultra-thin film manufacturing technologies for capacitor films, including copper and zinc compound deposition for enhanced reliability. It has developed ultra-thin capacitor films down to 2.3 microns for electric vehicles and renewable energy applications. The company also employs multilayer polyolefin film technology and has ongoing R&D projects for high-heat resistant films, recyclable all-PE gas barrier films, and eco-friendly PO wraps. Heavy industry production involves precision manufacturing of ship engine liners and related components.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Key customers include manufacturers of eco-friendly vehicles (BEV, HEV, PHEV, FCEV), renewable energy inverter producers, capacitor and electronic device manufacturers, food packaging companies, and shipbuilders. The capacitor films serve global markets including Europe, China, and the US. BOPP and WRAP films primarily serve domestic food packaging industries. Heavy industry products are supplied to major shipbuilders such as Hyundai Heavy Industries and engine manufacturers. The company also supplies domestic dairy companies for milk cartons until the segment's discontinuation.
categories.geographic_coverage: Samyoung operates mainly in South Korea with production facilities in Cheongju and formerly Gumi (now sold). It has a subsidiary in Vietnam producing PVC wrap films. Its sales and exports cover domestic markets and international markets including Europe, China, and the United States. The company is expanding its global footprint particularly in capacitor films for electric vehicles and renewable energy sectors.
categories.supply_chain_position: Samyoung operates primarily as a midstream manufacturer and supplier of specialized films and components. It produces core materials such as capacitor films and packaging films that are supplied to downstream manufacturers of capacitors, inverters, electric vehicles, and packaged food products. In heavy industry, it manufactures engine parts supplied directly to shipbuilders, positioning itself as a key component supplier in the industrial supply chain.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The company focuses strategically on expanding its capacitor film business, especially ultra-thin films for eco-friendly vehicles and renewable energy applications. R&D efforts target high-heat resistant films, recyclable and eco-friendly packaging films, and next-generation electronic films for secondary batteries. It invests in new production lines to increase capacity and improve cost competitiveness. The company also emphasizes quality improvement, diversification of customers, and development of high value-added products to enhance profitability.
categories.revenue_model: Samyoung generates revenue primarily through the manufacturing and sale of specialized films (capacitor, BOPP, WRAP) and heavy industry components. Revenue streams include domestic and export sales of products to industrial customers, food packaging companies, and shipbuilders. The company also had revenue from milk carton packaging until the business was discontinued in 2023. Revenue is based on product sales with payment terms typically on monthly billing cycles with cash or short-term notes.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: In the capacitor film market, Samyoung is the only domestic manufacturer and ranks third globally, competing with about 30 global producers, with only about five capable of producing ultra-thin films for eco-friendly vehicles. In BOPP films, it is the domestic market leader with a 17% market share. The heavy industry segment competes with a few global suppliers of ship engine liners. The company maintains a strong competitive position through technological leadership, quality, and production capacity expansion.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: As of 2023, Samyoung reported consolidated revenues of approximately 122.6 billion KRW, a 9.4% decrease from the previous year, with operating income increasing by 118% to 6 billion KRW. Net income surged by over 1600% to 18.6 billion KRW, largely due to asset sales including the Gumi plant. The company has about 34 million issued shares and maintains a relatively healthy debt ratio of 96.6%. It is undergoing a strategic shift focusing on high-growth capacitor film business while divesting non-core or loss-making segments.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Samyoung offers unique value through its status as the sole domestic and third-largest global producer of ultra-thin capacitor films critical for eco-friendly vehicles and renewable energy applications. Its products are characterized by high reliability, advanced ultra-thin technology, and cost competitiveness enabled by recent production line expansions. The company emphasizes quality, delivery stability, and innovation in eco-friendly packaging films (PO wrap) as well as high-performance films for secondary batteries, positioning itself as a technology leader in niche high-value markets.
